data.name: Gershon
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew words ger, meaning stranger or foreigner, and shachan, meaning man or warrior. In the Bible, Gershon is a son of Levi and the namesake of one of the three major clans of the tribe of Levi.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of courage and strength in faith.

in_hebrew.name: גֵרשוֹן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew root 'Garash' which means to level or clear. The name Gershon can be translated as 'hillman' or 'dweller on a level place'. In the Bible, the name Gershon is borne by one of the sons of Levi (Exodus 6:15).

in_greek.name: Γερσων
in_greek.long_meaning: Greek form of the Hebrew name Gershon. In the Septuagint (the ancient Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible), the name Gershon is transliterated as Γερσων (Gerson).

in_latin.name: Gershon
in_latin.long_meaning: Latin form of the Greek name Gershon. In medieval Europe, the name Gershon was adopted by Jews who had migrated from the Byzantine Empire. It is also found in some Latin texts as a transliteration of the Hebrew name.

in_english.name: Gershon
in_english.long_meaning: From the Hebrew name גֵרשוֹן (Gershon), which means 'Level, hill'. The name Gershon can be translated as 'hillman' or 'dweller on a level place'. In the Bible, the name Gershon is borne by one of the sons of Levi (Exodus 6:15).

biblical_reference.note: Name of a son of Levi and grandson of Jacob.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gershon is of Hebrew origin and carries cultural significance as a name given to children in Jewish communities. The name signifies that their ancestors were once foreigners or strangers in a land but have since become warriors or protectors of their faith and traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual sense, the name Gershon serves as a reminder of God's promise to the Israelites that He would make them a great nation and give them a land that was not theirs by birthright but through His divine intervention. It also reflects the proclamation in the Bible that, "The Lord your God is with you, He is mighty to save. He will take great delight in you, He will quiet you with His love, He will rejoice over you with singing." (Zephaniah 3:17) Ultimately, the name Gershon fosters a sense of identity as a chosen people, with a heritage of strength, resilience, and faith in the face of adversity.
